title: Follow-up to GCLI-121: quoted-annotation reader parity with the unquoted twin and fixture gaps (Opus round 1 non-blocking notes)
description: Non-blocking findings of Opus round 1 on opum-ai/glyph-cli#217 (landed as 3653b12). None is unsound. Measure every fixture delta against dev by running both.

acceptanceCriteria.text: F1: "None | None | C" resolves quoted (reader builds the pipe chain flat, calls.ts reference/expression) but refuses unquoted (tree-sitter nests left, None filter leaves 2 members): nest left or refuse more than one None, with a refused fixture and the unquoted twin asserted
F2a: the forward-reference test asserts callees as well as delta (app.py:C.meth, and the second qualname), confirmed
F2b: a fixture for the shape that produced the jinja and rich edges: class K: def m(self, o: "K"): o.meth()
F2c: a lexical-shadow fixture: module-level C plus a different function-local or class-body C

F3: decide and fixture the forms the unquoted twin accepts that the quoted form loses (conservative): "Optional[C] | None", "Union[C, None] | None", "None | Optional[C]", non-ASCII identifiers (QUOTED_NAME is ASCII-only), trailing comma Union[C, None,]
F4: confirm whether CPython ForwardRef rejects leading whitespace in " C | None " and fix the fixture accordingly; \s in QUOTED_NAME accepts U+00A0 in dotted names (nit)
F5 (nit): the triple-quote and escape guards in plainQuotedText are redundant with the reader, so those refusals cannot go red by mutating the guards: remove the redundancy or give each its own proof
F6 (nit): text.slice(pos) in reference() is quadratic on adversarial pipe chains: use a sticky regex
